questions.q:
Select the option that changes the degree of comparison in the given sentence from superlative to positive without changing the meaning of the sentence.


Kalpana Ahuja is the tallest girl in the colony.

[SSC MTS 2024]
o: No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja.
No other girl in the colony is as taller as Kalpana Ahuja.
Kalpana Ahuja is as tallest as other girls of the colony.
Many girls in the colony are taller than Kalpana Ahuja.
questions.s:
The correct answer is: No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja.


The original sentence "Kalpana Ahuja is the tallest girl in the colony" is in the superlative degree. It compares Kalpana's height to all other girls in the colony, stating that she is the most tall.

To change this into positive degree, we need to express the same idea without using the superlative form. The positive degree expresses equality or the lack of comparison, so we need a sentence that says no one else is as tall as Kalpana.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Bilingual children are so intelligent than those who speak just one language.
questions.s:
The underlined phrase "so intelligent than" is incorrect for a comparative structure. "More intelligent than" correctly uses "more" for the comparative degree of "intelligent" and "than" for comparison.

"So intelligent to"-Incorrect because "so" is not used with "to" in comparisons; it requires "that" in different structures.

"Better intelligent than"-Incorrect because "better" is the comparative form of "good," not "intelligent." The correct form is "more intelligent."

"The most intelligent to"-Incorrect because "the most" is superlative, not comparative, and "to" is not used in comparisons.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Note:

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

questions.q:
The wedding gown / looked decently / despite being / studded wit jewels.

{CGL PRE 09/12/2022 S3}
questions.s: The adverb "decently" is incorrectly used in the sentence. The correct adjective to describe how the wedding gown looked should be "decent," not "decently." "Decently" is an adverb that modifies verbs, not adjectives. In this case, we need an adjective to describe the noun "gown.”

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Tia wanted a dog that was _________ than Larry's dog.
questions.s:
When two entities (person or things) are being compared then 'comparative degree' is used, here Tia's imaginary dog is compared with Larry's dog. Therefore, the use of 'smarter and stronger' is the right phrase for the blank.

The complete sentence is- 'Tia wanted a dog that was smarter and stronger than Larry's dog.'

Hence, option (c) is correct.

NOTE/-

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.
